report.summary: Chunk 1 of gated_writes.py: module docstring, rebase functions, GatedCandidate, artifact_root, relay gate, recording runner, provider receipt, spec_for stub.
risks: _relay_gate | medium | The gate reads box['result'] which is set by _recording_runner; if execution order changes in TaskAttempt, the gate might read stale data. This is a claim that the runner runs before the gate; we can't verify that here.
_artifact_root_for | low | Uses LOCALAPPDATA or tempdir; on systems where LOCALAPPDATA is not set, it falls back to tempdir. This is acceptable but worth noting.

claims.text: This module does not repeat any of that. It has two responsibilities: PHASE 1 -- CONCURRENT GATING (gate_candidates). ... PHASE 2 -- PROMOTION (promote_candidates; opt-in, a separate call, NOT wired into KairosScheduler.dispatch()'s default path -- see daedalus/kairos/scheduler.py). PHASE 3 -- SEALED HANDOFF (run_write_wave).
claims.why: The functions gate_candidates, promote_candidates, run_write_wave are not defined in this chunk; the module's responsibility claims cannot be verified against this code alone.

claims.text: An absolute path that resolves under primary_root is rebased to its repo-relative form. An absolute path that resolves OUTSIDE primary_root is returned unchanged
claims.why: The function implementation (lines 116-123) does exactly that: if p.is_absolute() and can be made relative to primary_root, return relative; otherwise return raw.

claims.text: A held candidate cannot live only in AttemptResult.artifact: run_write_wave returns plain dictionaries and TaskAttempt reaps its candidate branch, so those bytes otherwise disappear as soon as the call returns.
claims.why: The claim about TaskAttempt reaping branches and run_write_wave returning dicts refers to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: _relay_gate: A gate callable only ever receives a RunnerContext (worktree/branch/base/task/is_cancelled) -- never the runner's return value -- so there is no direct way to ask 'did offload() call this clean'. box is a mutable cell the paired runner (_recording_runner) writes its result into before returning; this closure reads it back.
claims.why: The claim about RunnerContext contents and the execution order (runner before gate) refers to daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This still catches a real failure mode a bare 'is the diff non-empty' check would miss: offload can finish with action == 'escalated_after_verify_fail' while wrote is NON-EMPTY, because a write it could not fully roll back is reported in dirty_unreverted and kept in wrote so it stays visible. That leaves a non-empty artifact for a run offload itself considers FAILED, and only checking action == 'offloaded' (not 'artifact exists') refuses it.
claims.why: The claim about offload's behavior (action values, dirty_unreverted) refers to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: Returns (runner, box). box['result'] is set the instant the runner returns, which is always BEFORE TaskAttempt calls the gate (see daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger: runner, then artifact capture, then gate) -- so _relay_gate reading box always sees this attempt's own result, never a stale or missing one.
claims.why: The claim about TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger execution order refers to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: The full provider result lives on AttemptResult.runner_detail. The write-wave projection used to drop it, collapsing every provider refusal into 'the runner produced no change to gate'. Keep only routing/action facts, measured writes, and rewrite activation/skip provenance -- never prompts, repository content, or arbitrary model prose.
claims.why: The claim about AttemptResult.runner_detail and previous behavior refers to code outside this chunk.
The function name and signature match the docstring's description.

observations.what: The module docstring describes three phases but the chunk only defines Phase 1 helpers. Phase 2 and 3 functions are not present.
_spec_for is a stub with no implementation in this chunk.
_relay_gate and _recording_runner rely on execution order guarantees from TaskAttempt that are not verifiable here.
